set.n: Vejvoda's buried silver, farm NE of Rice Lake
set.pl: Vejvoda farm northeast of Rice Lake (placeholder until the farm is placed on a 1914-1930s Barron County plat)
set.st: A Barron County farmer, on the place since about 1897, hid his savings in sacks and in the ground. After his wife died in July 1925 about $6,000 was recovered: a flour sack, a poppy-seed sack, some buried, and more than $1,000 in an old coat ruined by mice. He said "there is a large quantity of silver buried between the road and the house." No later dig or find was reported 1925-35. Pin is a placeholder, not the farm.
set.v: About $6,000 recovered; "a large quantity of silver" said to be buried between the road and the house
set.t: Search the strip between the farm's road frontage and the old house site; check the 1938 aerial for the house and driveway. Provisional C: becomes B once the farm is placed on a plat. Private farm: permission needed.
pinev: Placeholder northeast of Rice Lake (about 3 km) until the farm is placed
Two separate accounts (Eau Claire Leader-Telegram and Baraboo News-Republic, Oct 1925)
